newsitem.title: UK: UK group wants more power generation competition.
newsitem.headline: UK group wants more power generation competition.

text.p: A British electricity consumers lobby group called on Tuesday for increased competition in generation to bring down prices when the market is liberalised in 1998.

The Electricity Consumers' Committee Chairmen's Group (ECCCG), launching its annual report, said that despite participation by new generators, there was still not enough competition and that prices were mostly set by National Power Plc and PowerGen Plc.
It said that it was pushing for an end to capacity payments in the Pool, or wholesale, electricity market, and changes in the bidding system.
"Attention must now focus on the market power of generators and Pool pricing issues to bring down prices for all in 1998," ECCCG chairman Yvonne Constance said in a statement.
The ECCCG is also pushing for lower prices even for consumers who do not switch supplier when the market opens up.
The ECCCG also supports tighter financial and accounting requirements in takeovers and more powers for the Regulator to monitor the results.
Electricity Consumers' Committees were established in 1990 after privatisation of the regional electricity companies (Recs) to represent the interests of consumers.
The chairmen are appointed by the regulator, Offer, in consultation with the government. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
